datasets.name: ds_kpi
queryLines: SELECT c.event_date, c.impressions, c.clicks, c.conversions, c.spend_usd, c.conversion_value_usd,
SELECT event_date, SUM(impressions) AS impressions, SUM(clicks) AS clicks,
SUM(conversions) AS conversions, SUM(spend_usd) AS spend_usd,
SELECT p.event_date, SUM(p.spend_usd * greatest(0, 1 - p.actual_ctr / nullif(b.baseline_ctr, 0))) AS wasted_spend_usd
JOIN (SELECT campaign_id, SUM(clicks) / SUM(impressions) AS baseline_ctr FROM gold_segment_ctr_daily WHERE is_drift_window = FALSE GROUP BY campaign_id) b
WHERE p.is_drift_window = TRUE AND p.is_drift_segment = TRUE GROUP BY p.event_date

datasets.name: ds_pred_actual
datasets.displayName: Predicted vs actual CTR by week
queryLines: SELECT date_trunc('week', event_date) AS event_week, impressions,
) GROUP BY event_week ORDER BY event_week

datasets.name: ds_channel_mix
queryLines: GROUP BY event_week, event_date, channel ORDER BY event_week, channel

datasets.name: ds_segment_gap
queryLines: SELECT p.event_date, p.channel, p.device, p.country, p.visitor_type, p.campaign_name, p.objective,
THEN p.spend_usd * greatest(0, 1 - p.actual_ctr / nullif(b.baseline_ctr, 0)) ELSE 0 END AS wasted_spend_usd
LEFT JOIN (SELECT campaign_id, SUM(clicks) / SUM(impressions) AS baseline_ctr FROM gold_segment_ctr_daily WHERE is_drift_window = FALSE GROUP BY campaign_id) b

datasets.name: ds_health_latest
queryLines: SELECT metric_date, model_version, actual_ctr, predicted_ctr, weighted_rmse, weighted_mae, signed_bias, absolute_ctr_gap, baseline_rmse, rmse_change_pct, drift_status, observation_count, impressions FROM gold_model_monitoring_metrics WHERE dimension_name = 'overall' AND dimension_value = 'All' AND window_days = 7 AND metric_date = (SELECT MAX(metric_date) FROM gold_model_monitoring_metrics)

datasets.name: ds_health_trend
queryLines: SELECT metric_date, actual_ctr, predicted_ctr, weighted_rmse, weighted_mae, baseline_rmse, rmse_change_pct, drift_status FROM gold_model_monitoring_metrics WHERE dimension_name = 'overall' AND dimension_value = 'All' AND window_days = 7 ORDER BY metric_date

datasets.name: ds_health_slices
queryLines: SELECT metric_date, dimension_name, dimension_value, CONCAT(dimension_name, ': ', dimension_value) AS slice_name, model_version, actual_ctr, predicted_ctr, weighted_rmse, weighted_mae, signed_bias, absolute_ctr_gap, baseline_rmse, rmse_change_pct, drift_status, observation_count, impressions FROM gold_model_monitoring_metrics WHERE dimension_name <> 'overall' AND window_days = 7 AND metric_date = (SELECT MAX(metric_date) FROM gold_model_monitoring_metrics)

datasets.name: ds_retrain_decisions
queryLines: SELECT evaluated_at, metric_date, weighted_rmse, baseline_rmse, rmse_change_pct, impressions, should_retrain, reason FROM model_retrain_decisions ORDER BY evaluated_at DESC

# NorthPeak Goods — CTR Optimization: Spend & Drift

**What happened:** three weeks ago marketing shifted budget from Search to **Social + Display** (impression share jumped from ~20% to ~50%). Those prospecting/awareness segments reach colder audiences, so their true CTR collapsed — but the **stale production model** kept predicting the old ~2.4% rate, so the bidding system over-bid and burned **~$242K**.

**On this page:** the top line shows the stale model's prediction (orange) staying flat while actual CTR (navy) falls — that widening gap is the wasted spend. The area chart shows the Social/Display mix swelling; the bars show where CTR collapsed and where the waste concentrated.

frame.title: Predicted (stale) vs actual CTR — the divergence
Weekly impressions by channel — the mix shift
CTR by channel — Social & Display lowest
Wasted spend by channel — Social & Display dominate

lines:
# Model & Recovery — the retrained champion

Maya reran the **standardized batch training workflow**: engineer feature sets → train XGBoost CTR-regression candidates → tune with Optuna → log every run to **MLflow** → register the winner in **Unity Catalog** and promote the **`@champion`** alias. The champion learned the new Social/Display reality, so its predictions track actual CTR again.

**On this page:** the top line shows the champion (cyan) snapping onto actual CTR (navy) even through the drift window, where the stale model (orange) stayed wrong. The gap bars quantify the fix per channel, and the table lists the exact mis-bid segments the retrain corrected. The MLflow experiment leaderboard + feature importance are shown live in the notebook.

frame.title: Champion tracks actual CTR; stale model stayed wrong
Prediction gap by channel: stale (orange) vs champion (cyan)
CTR-accuracy lift by channel — biggest on Social & Display
Worst mis-bid segments (sorted by stale gap)

# Model Health — drift, accuracy, and automated retraining

The same impression-weighted metrics drive this dashboard and the daily retraining decision. **Warning:** RMSE ≥10% above baseline. **Critical:** RMSE ≥20% above baseline. Retraining requires two consecutive critical 7-day periods, at least 50K impressions, and a 7-day cooldown.
Select **channel, device, country, visitor type, campaign, or objective** to compare the latest 7-day accuracy. The scatter highlights slices where RMSE deterioration and absolute CTR error coincide.
